pairs.question: Quid huc seniles fessa moliris gradus, o fida nutrix, turbidam frontem gerens et maesta uultu? sospes est certe parens sospesque Phaedra stirpis et geminae iugum?
pairs.answer: Metus remitte, prospero regnum in statu est domusque florens sorte felici uiget.
pairs.derivation: Hippolytus' entire speech is one anxious question to the Nurse (why this troubled approach; is parent and Phaedra safe?), quoted verbatim and contiguous. Stripped speaker labels 'Hippolytvs'/'Nvt.' and the inline verse number 435. Answer is the Nurse's operative first response ('set aside fear; the kingdom prospers'); cut at 'uiget.' (first full stop) before she turns to elaborating ('sed tu beatis mitior rebus ueni... namque anxiam me cura sollicitat tui').

pairs.question: Cur omnium fit culpa paucarum scelus?
pairs.derivation: Nurse asks why the crime of a few becomes the fault of all; Hippolytus answers that he does indeed loathe them all. Stripped speaker labels 'Nvt.'/'Hi.' and inline verse number 565. Answer cut at 'execror.' (first full stop) before the elaboration 'sit ratio, sit natura, sit dirus furor...'.
